narrator.how: an English storyteller of the 1880s reading aloud by the fire: urbane, dry, gently mocking, every sentence turned like a joke at dinner; under the wit, now and then, a quiet sadness

virginia.how: an American girl of fifteen: light, quick and free; says hard things straight out, short, as a question to the face; flares up childishly when the weak are laughed at; tender and very quiet when moved, hiding that she is near tears

simon.how: a three-hundred-year-old ghost and an old actor: grand, pompous, theatrical, rolling his words, wounded pride in every phrase; when no one is watching, a very tired old man, hoarse and slow

otis.how: the American Minister: impeccably polite, slow, even and reasonable; the more trying things are, the slower and politer he speaks; never raises his voice; warm with his daughter

washington.how: the eldest son, a cheerful handsome young American: jokes about everything, quick and sure of himself; when something touches him, suddenly serious and short

mrs_otis.how: a healthy, practical American mother: brisk, warm, sensible, a little amused; brooks no nonsense

twin_star.how: a boy of ten, one of the twins: loud, excited, mischievous, shouting and laughing over his brother

twin_stripes.how: a boy of ten, the other twin: bright, cheeky, teasing in a sing-song, breathless with fun

mrs_umney.how: an old English housekeeper in black silk and a white cap: low, hushed and solemn; she believes in the ghost and remembers when everyone here was afraid

voices.how: many voices in the dark beyond the wall, whispering together, breathy and cold, pleading and wicked at once

cecil.how: the young Duke of Cheshire, fifteen and in love: shy, warm and plain; says little and asks nothing more than he must
